task.name: Every audit record reports the same hardcoded forge version, so run provenance is unrecoverable
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

Every audit record forge writes carries `"forge_version": "0.1.0"`, regardless
of the version that actually produced the run.

Verified in this repository across runs written by `0.13.0rc11`
(`e8f80be90876`, `a0adedafb785`, `9bf3a54703f3`) and in an adopter repository
across thirteen runs spanning 2026-07-23 to 2026-07-29, produced by pinned
versions ranging from `0.13.0rc6` through `0.13.0rc10`. All twenty-plus records
read `0.1.0`. `forge version` itself reports the installed version correctly, so
the runtime knows what it is; the audit writer does not ask.

The operator consequence surfaced while diagnosing adopter sprint failures: given
a failed run, there is no way to tell whether it was produced by a build that
predates a fix that was already shipped, which is the first question a failure
triage asks.

## Expected behavior

A provenance field on an audit record must reflect the runtime that produced that
record. Version is what lets an operator decide whether an old failure is still
live or was already fixed, and it is what any downstream consumer would condition
on when deciding whether a historical run should still be trusted or taught from.
A provenance field that cannot vary is worse than an absent one, because a
consumer reading it cannot distinguish a real answer from a constant, and will
draw conclusions from it either way.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** all audit records claim forge version `0.1.0`, in every
  repository, under every installed version.

- **Evidence:** `src/theforge/coordinator/audit.py:627` writes the string
  literal `"forge_version": "0.1.0"` into the record. The value is read back and
  propagated to downstream records at `src/theforge/cli/shared.py:314`,
  `src/theforge/cli/shared.py:322`, `src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:141`, and
  `src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:147`, so the constant reaches every consumer of
  the audit substrate rather than staying local to the writer.

- **Ruled out:** not a failed version lookup — nothing at the write site attempts
  to detect the running version, so there is no detection path that could be
  failing or falling back. Not a schema-migration artifact; `schema_version` is a
  separate field and is populated.

- **Confirmed cause:** the version is a hardcoded literal at the single audit
  write site.

- **Affected code path:** `coordinator/audit.py` (write site);
  `cli/shared.py` and `sprint/audit.py` (propagation to derived records).

- **Fix-success criterion:** a run executed under a given installed version
  writes that version into its audit record, a run under a different version
  writes the different version, and no code path emits a version constant.

## Notes

This bears on the audit-substrate ADR's provenance obligations, and on any
filtering that would exclude historical runs by the version that produced them —
such filtering currently reads a constant and would silently match everything or
nothing.

handoff.summary: Fixed the audit record writer at coordinator/audit.py:633 which hardcoded `"forge_version": "0.1.0"` for every run regardless of installed version. Replaced the literal with `theforge.__version__` (already exposed via importlib.metadata in src/theforge/__init__.py), imported as `FORGE_VERSION`. Propagation sites (cli/shared.py, sprint/audit.py) already read the field via .get() and needed no changes since they just forward whatever value is in the source record. Added a regression test verifying the written forge_version matches theforge.__version__ and is not the old constant.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
